title: Leon Rappolo and Leon Prima joining Kelley in Houston
summary: Prima and Rappolo joined the Houston band around 1924; Rappolo as a faker clarinetist influencing jazz clarinet.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: I was wondering about, uh, rap. When did you first meet Leon Rapolo?

When I was with Peck Kelly, we needed a clarinetist over in Houston, and, uh, we needed a trumpet player, too. We got Leon Rapolo, and we got Leon Prima first, who was the trumpet player. And then, uh, he recommended Leon Rapolo. And Leon Rapolo came over and worked with us over at Houston.

About 1924. Which was one of the last jobs, I guess, Rapolo played before he lost his health. He was over there, and he was a wonderful clarinetist. Strictly a faker. He didn't read, I know. And, uh, but it was the beginning of, uh, jazz clarinet. Benny Goodman and all of them. Heard him when he went to Chicago with the New Orleans Rhythm Kings. And, uh, of course, right away, they, uh, that gave them the idea of what a clarinet should sound like. And with their technique, but went with it, that's what made those kids so wonderful.
Now, uh, how did Leon Prima play in those years? Very good.
